solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wood drill included in limited bargain offer

indicators.note: something included in another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a sale is a bargain offer that runs for a limited time
PE, physical education, is school drill or exercise

explanation.surface: A shop runs a short promotion on power tools, with a drill thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood drill' reads as a tool for boring timber; drill is really school exercise, PE. SAPELE is an African hardwood like mahogany.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapele is a reddish African hardwood tree and its timber, used for furniture and veneers.

clue.text: Slippery sort of trick, entering country after cover’s blown

indicators.note: when a cover is blown the top is lost, so the opening letter goes
something entering goes inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: CANADA with its first letter removed
a con is a trick or swindle

explanation.surface: A slippery operator slips into a country after their spy cover is exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover's blown' sounds like espionage; here the cover is the top letter of the country, which comes off before the trick goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake is a proverbially slippery creature, and the anaconda is a large South American constricting serpent.

clue.text: What’s said to turn heads yet feels wrong

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of their proper order and must be rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something said to make people look round still leaves you feeling uneasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn heads' suggests glamour; here it is literal, a parade-ground order to look to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: On parade, the command for soldiers to turn their heads sharply towards the left, usually in salute while marching past.

clue.text: Will nominee from 60 per cent of business chiefs run with current vote?

indicators.note: sixty per cent means keeping only six of every ten letters from the start

blocks.note: EXECUTIVES has ten letters; the first six are kept
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
I is the symbol for electric current
a voter marks a ballot with a cross

explanation.surface: A question about company bosses' choice in an election, framed as a will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like the future tense, but it is a testament; 'with' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An executrix is a woman appointed in a testament to carry out its terms after the testator's death.

clue.text: American jazz slang Jack and I examine with a vacant look

indicators.note: something vacant is emptied, so only its outside letters remain

blocks.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
taken as written
to vet is to examine closely
taken as written
the word emptied of its middle

explanation.surface: Two people puzzle over American jazz slang, staring blankly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A vacant look' reads as a blank stare; it is A plus the shell of the word 'look'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jive talk was the hip argot of 1930s and 1940s Harlem jazz musicians, full of coded street expressions.

clue.text: My US off-road vehicle primarily evades roads, scaring woodland birds

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so each word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: the Jeep is the American off-road vehicle
first letters of the three words
treecreepers, small birds that climb tree trunks, are called creepers

explanation.surface: An American off-roader swerves off the roads and frightens birds in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive attached to the vehicle; it is the exclamation of surprise, and 'US' qualifies both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise or alarm; the longer phrase is a dated American expletive used in place of 'Jesus Christ'.

clue.text: Joy caught good man cutting a piece of cake

indicators.note: a blade cutting into something goes inside it, so these letters are set within the others

blocks.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
ST, saint, is a crossword good man
a piece of cake is something easy

explanation.surface: Joy is caught by a decent man slicing a bit of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A piece of cake' tempts a literal slice; it is the idiom for something simple.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is an overwhelming feeling of delight or rapture, the extreme of happiness.

clue.text: Aesthetically pleasing strict AI hybrid

indicators.note: a hybrid is a mixture, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rigid artificial intelligence blended with something attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hybrid' sounds like a description of the AI system; it signals the letters are blended.
explanation.definitionFit: Something artistic shows creative skill and taste, and is attractive to look at.

clue.text: Jumper and anorak go astray

indicators.note: things gone astray have wandered from their places, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sweater and a waterproof coat go missing from the laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumper is British for a sweater, and with 'anorak' it looks like clothing; it is an animal that jumps. 'And' just joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Kangaroos move by hopping on their powerful hind legs, making them the archetypal leaping animal.

clue.text: Me Too movement’s crux is about stopping a sheer lunatic

indicators.note: the crux is the heart of a matter, so the central letters are taken
to be about is to turn round, so the letters run the other way
a stopping plugs a gap, so this piece goes inside the other
lunatic means crazy, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the two central letters of the eight-letter word
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The key point of the #MeToo campaign is about halting an utterly mad person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Me Too movement' reads as the campaign, but 'Me Too' alone is the definition, the casual reply of someone who agrees; 'movement' only supplies its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are casual replies meaning the speaker shares the same experience or feeling as the previous person.

clue.text: British ballet luminary remains tense over Nureyev’s lead

indicators.note: the lead is what goes in front, so the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: ash is what remains after burning
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for over
opening letter of the dancer's name

explanation.surface: A great British dancer's legacy stays strained under Nureyev's leading role.
explanation.walkthrough: Over is O from cricket scoring, where an over is a set of six balls. Nureyev fits the ballet scene but supplies only N.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Frederick Ashton was the founding choreographer of the Royal Ballet and a towering figure of twentieth-century British dance.

clue.text: 23 city to fail in discussions

definitions.note: 23 Across is EUROPEAN, so a European city

indicators.note: discussions are spoken, so the words are taken by their sound

blocks.note: to fail is to lose, said out loud

explanation.surface: A European city's negotiations are about to collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference makes the definition 'European city'; 'to fail' is 'to lose', and spoken, that phrase matches the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Toulouse is a major city in south-west France, home of the Airbus aircraft industry.

clue.text: Revolutionary Dadaist affair involves Ivy’s family member

indicators.note: to involve is to contain, so the run of letters lies inside the words
a revolution turns things round, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: a run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A radical avant-garde artist's love affair draws in a relative called Ivy.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivy looks like a woman's name; it is the plant, and its family is the Araliaceae. The letters sit backwards across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatsia, the false castor-oil plant, belongs to the same botanical family, Araliaceae, as common ivy.

clue.text: Rope lines missing on bar linked to back of pulley

indicators.note: what is missing has gone, so those letters are removed
the back of something is its end, so the final letter is taken

blocks.note: to forestall is to bar or prevent
L is the abbreviation for line, so two of them
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A rope with missing lines hangs from a rod attached to a pulley.
explanation.walkthrough: FORESTALL loses its two Ls (lines), then Y is added. The sailing setting makes 'lines' look like ropes, but it is just LL.
explanation.definitionFit: A forestay is the stay, or supporting wire rope, running from a sailing ship's masthead down to the bow.

clue.text: Severe critic of, on and off, adroit formality

indicators.note: on and off means every other time, so alternate letters are kept

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters
starch is stiffness or formality of manner

explanation.surface: A harsh reviewer of clever stiffness that comes and goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The name comes from Aristarchus of Samothrace, a famously exacting Greek scholar who edited Homer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aristarch is a rare word for a stern, exacting reviewer, after the ancient Alexandrian textual scholar.

clue.text: Orient Express, without stopping around Vienna, finally heading for Turkey

indicators.note: a stopping is a dental filling, so the word loses its filling and keeps only its shell
finally points to the end, so the last letter is taken
to go around is to surround, so one piece is placed within another
a heading sits at the top, so the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: the word with its inside emptied out
last letter of the city
the heading, or first letter, of the word

explanation.surface: The Orient Express runs non-stop past Vienna and finally makes for Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orient Express' is the famous train, but Orient alone is the definition. A stopping is an old word for a tooth filling. 'Heading for' gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient is the eastern world, and as a noun the word names the direction of sunrise.

clue.text: Hard cheese, Sparks, pulled up over ridiculous slang

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulling up makes letters read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: Sparks is the setter, who refers to themselves as me
mental is slang for crazy or absurd

explanation.surface: Bad luck, Sparks: you've been told off for using silly slang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard cheese' is British slang for bad luck, which makes the start look like a commiseration; Emmental is in fact a hard cheese. 'Over' places the reversed piece on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmental is a firm Swiss cheese with large holes, classed among the hard cheeses.

clue.text: Highly respectable senior copper held up by bigotry intermittently

indicators.note: intermittently means at intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: a super is a superintendent, a senior police officer
second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A distinguished senior policeman is delayed by occasional prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer one piece is held up, or supported, by the piece below it, so 'held up' is placement, not delay.
explanation.definitionFit: Superior can mean of high standing or quality, deserving esteem, as in a superior class of hotel.

clue.text: Imitate Italian novelist penning hardback’s intro

indicators.note: an intro is the opening, so the first letter is taken
to pen is to enclose, so one piece is shut inside another

blocks.note: Umberto Eco wrote The Name of the Rose
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Copy an Italian author writing the introduction to a hardback edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penning' fits the writer, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo someone is to repeat or copy their words or manner, much like a reflected sound.

clue.text: Free at last, Haiti desperately welcoming work for country

indicators.note: at last points to the end, so the final letter is taken
acting desperately is acting wildly, so these letters are thrown about
to welcome is to take in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: final letter of the word
the letters to be rearranged
OP, opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Finally liberated, Haiti eagerly takes on jobs for the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Haiti looks like the country wanted, but it is only anagram material; the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethiopia is a nation in the Horn of Africa, with Addis Ababa as its capital.

clue.text: One’s ground worthless part of diamond?

blocks.note: one's home ground, where one lives
base means low or of little value, as in base metal

explanation.surface: A cut gem's dust turns out to be the valueless fraction of a diamond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's ground' and 'diamond' suggest grinding a jewel; the diamond is a baseball field, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the infield is called the diamond, and home plate, where runs score, sits at one corner.

clue.text: Who might get you to live, quelling ogre?

indicators.note: to quell is to hold down and subdue, so one piece is kept pinned inside another

blocks.note: to exist is to live
an orc is a fantasy ogre or monster

explanation.surface: A question about who might save your life by subduing a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a fairy-tale rescue; the definition casts 'you' as a demon, whom this person would 'get' by driving it out.
explanation.definitionFit: An exorcist expels evil spirits, so if you were a possessing demon this is the person who would come after you.

clue.text: Non-British native of Bangladesh expressing a quiet language

indicators.note: non- means without, so the abbreviation for British is dropped
to express is to squeeze out, so a letter is pressed out of the word

blocks.note: a Bengali is from Bengal, which includes Bangladesh
the letter squeezed out
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A Bangladeshi with no British ties speaking a hushed language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expressing' looks like speaking, but here it means pressing out, so a letter is squeezed from the word. Bengal spans Bangladesh and part of India.
explanation.definitionFit: English is a language, the tongue of England now spoken worldwide.

clue.text: What is somehow in conclusion ideally green?

definitions.text: What is somehow in conclusion ideally green?

indicators.note: a conclusion is the end, so the final letter is taken
somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters come in some new order

blocks.note: final letter of the word
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about what, ideally, ought to be eco-friendly in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue asks what should ideally be green; the wordplay shuffles GREEN with the last letter of 'ideally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Renewable power from wind, sun or water is called green energy, the thing campaigners want to be sustainable.

clue.text: Wound counterpart, ultimately brave in death

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the last letter is taken
something in another sits within it, so these pieces go inside

blocks.note: a twin is an exact counterpart
final letter of the word
death is one's end

explanation.surface: An injury to a partner, who finally faces death bravely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' looks like an injury (rhyming with 'tuned'); it is the past tense of wind, as in twisted.
explanation.definitionFit: Entwined means twisted or coiled together, as strands are when they have been wound round each other.

clue.text: Dim idiot swallows lithium

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a twit is a fool
Li is the chemical symbol for lithium

explanation.surface: A dim-witted fool gulps down a lithium pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dim' seems to describe the idiot's intelligence; it is the definition, meaning poorly lit.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilit describes the faint half-light of dusk, so a scene that is twilit is gloomy and shadowy.

clue.text: Say 19 Down to be sorry for backing article in public

definitions.note: 19 Down is ENGLISH; an English person is, for example, a European

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
one thing in another sits inside it, so this piece is placed within

blocks.note: to rue is to regret
something public is open
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An English person apologising in public for supporting a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' flags the definition as an example: an English person is one kind of European. 'Article' looks like a news piece; it is A.
explanation.definitionFit: England is in Europe, so an English person is a typical example of a European by nationality.

clue.text: Holding chain, those who entice dogs

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece contains the other

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for chain, an old unit of length
people who lure others in

explanation.surface: People who tempt dogs while holding a chain lead.
explanation.walkthrough: A lurcher is a British crossbreed of greyhound and working dog, once used by poachers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurchers are crossbred hunting animals, typically sighthound mixed with collie or terrier.

clue.text: Retreat in which you’ll find the essence of freedom?

definitions.text: Retreat in which you’ll find the essence of freedom?

indicators.note: a place in which something is found holds it inside
the essence is the core, so the central letter is taken

blocks.note: a haven is a refuge or retreat
central letter of the seven-letter word

explanation.surface: A question about a sanctuary that embodies the very idea of liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, a final refuge of perfect freedom, while also building it.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is imagined as the ultimate sanctuary where the soul is released from earthly bonds and suffering.
